#   ConfigServer Threat Database › All Protocols › 1 Day
#   
#   These blocklists are maintained directly by ConfigServer and are
#   compiled from connection attempts against our honeypots, as well
#   as unauthorized access attempts targeting services we operate.
#   
#   The threat feeds capture malicious activity across a range of
#   exposed network services, including SSH, FTP, Telnet, VNC, SIP,
#   HTTP, RDP, SMTP, and similar internet-facing protocols.
#   
#   IP addresses included in these blocklists have been observed
#   engaging in behaviors such as brute force attempts, credential
#   stuffing, vulnerability scanning, automated exploitation, and
#   unauthorized access attempts against monitored systems.
#   
#   Blocklists prefixed with `_1d` represent activity observed within
#   the most recent 24-hour period. These entries reflect confirmed
#   connection attempts recorded during that window and are treated
#   as high-confidence indicators of malicious activity.
#   
#   Blocklists prefixed with `_365d` are cumulative datasets covering
#   a one-year period and may include a higher rate of false positives
#   due to IP reuse, NAT, and infrastructure changes across providers.
#   
#   The `all` blocklist aggregates observed connection attempts across
#   all monitored services, combining IP addresses identified through
#   SSH, FTP, VNC, RDP, SIP, and other tracked protocols into a single
#   unified dataset.
